visual_evidence: Four red 3D-printed rectangular bar pieces resting on a wooden surface, with the upper two pieces forming a fractured rectangular bar
Jagged, stepped fracture surface on the top of the upright upper-right piece exposing thin outer perimeter walls and an internal cross-patterned infill with empty cavities
Matching angled, rough break at the right end of the horizontal upper-left piece with a smooth semicircular hole or cutout edge visible along the fracture rim
Slight pale stress-whitening along the sharp broken wall tips on the upright upper-right piece
Fine FDM print lines visible along the matte red exterior faces of all four pieces
diagnosis.probable_cause: A single bending or impact load exceeded what the thin outer perimeters and hollow sparse infill could carry, causing a brittle-looking cross-layer snap initiated near the cutout in the middle of the bar.
alternative_modes: Bolt-hole tear-out pulls a local plug from a hole to an adjacent edge while the rest of the bar stays intact, whereas here the entire rectangular cross-section fractured completely across.

solutions.title: Increase perimeter walls and local infill
solutions.description: Increase outer perimeter count from ~2 walls to 5 or 6 walls and raise infill density to 60 to 100% across the middle ~20 mm of the bar using a slicer modifier.
pros: Uses 5 to 6 perimeters instead of ~2, eliminating the hollow core at the break
Requires no CAD changes or alterations to mating parts
Applies 60 to 100% infill only in the ~20 mm middle zone
cons: Adds ~5 to 10 min of print time per part

solutions.title: Relocate or reinforce the cutout
solutions.description: Move the hole or cutout out of the high-load middle region of the ~65 mm bar, or add a raised boss with extra perimeters around the opening.
pros: Removes the geometric discontinuity from the middle of the ~65 mm span
Keeps the ~12 mm by ~10 mm outer cross-section unchanged
cons: Requires editing the CAD model and mating hole locations
Adds ~5 min of print time if a boss is added

solutions.title: Thicken the bar cross-section
solutions.description: Increase the rectangular cross-section from ~12 mm wide by ~10 mm thick to ~15 mm wide by ~15 mm thick along the ~65 mm length.
pros: Expands the cross-section from ~12 mm by ~10 mm to ~15 mm by ~15 mm
Uses the same filament and standard slicer profiles
cons: Requires ~5 mm of extra clearance in the surrounding assembly
Adds ~10 min of print time per part

section_computed.basis: Same material, length and load. Weight scales with cross-section area. Bending strength scales with the section modulus (diameter cubed for a round section; width x thickness squared for a rectangle bent across its thickness). Stiffness scales with the second moment of area (diameter to the fourth; width x thickness cubed). These are ratios for the same load, not stress-concentration values: holes, notches and sharp corners are not included.

solutions.title: Switch to PETG filament
solutions.description: Reprint the part in PETG instead of rigid PLA so it yields before snapping under sudden loads or impacts.
pros: Deforms further before fracturing compared to rigid PLA
Prints on open-frame desktop FDM printers without an enclosure
cons: Requires ~235 to 245 °C nozzle and ~75 to 80 °C bed temperatures
Absorbs moisture and can string if not dried at ~50 °C

geometric_features: Semicircular hole or cutout edge right at the fracture on the upper-left piece
Sharp 90-degree exterior edges along the rectangular bar cross-section

rejected_alternative.visual_feature: Jagged, stepped fracture surface on the top of the upright upper-right piece exposing thin outer perimeter walls and an internal cross-patterned infill with empty cavities
rejected_alternative.reason: Layer delamination separates cleanly and flatly along a single layer boundary showing intact rounded extrusion bead tops, whereas this fracture cuts unevenly through the walls and exposes the internal infill structure.

diagnosis.mode_source: Ahn, Montero, Odell, Roundy & Wright, "Anisotropic material properties of fused deposition modeling ABS", Rapid Prototyping Journal 8(4), 2002
diagnosis.summary: The 3D-printed bar snapped across its hollow, sparsely infilled section because thin outer walls and a cutout could not handle the load.
